identification.name: ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene)
identification.common_form_notes: FDM filament available in 1.75 mm and 2.85 mm diameters. Sheet stock available in various thicknesses.
identification.notes: Properties represent bulk injection-moulded ABS (acrylonitrile butadiene styrene, medium impact grade per AZoM). Young's modulus (tensile) and glass transition temperature are not listed on the AZoM reference page; 2.1 GPa is a standard tensile E for ABS and Tg = 105 °C is a widely published value. FDM (fused deposition modeling)-printed parts have significantly lower strength (typically 50–80% of bulk) and are anisotropic — inter-layer (Z-axis) strength is typically 40–60% of in-plane (XY) strength. Requires an enclosure to prevent warping on large prints. Emits styrene fumes during printing — ventilate or use an enclosure with filtration. usable_temp_range max corrected from 70 °C to 89 °C (2026-08-02): the prior value used AZoM's separate "Max. Operating Temp." field for this grade, which was inconsistent with this same AZoM page's own heat deflection temperature (HDT) figures (98 °C @ 0.45 MPa, 89 °C @ 1.80 MPa) and made ABS appear less heat-resistant than PETG in this database — the reverse of ABS's well-established real-world behavior (ABS's Tg of ~105 °C and HDT of ~95–100 °C are both meaningfully higher than PETG's ~80 °C Tg and ~65–80 °C HDT; this is part of why enclosed-chamber printer designs such as Voron favor ABS/ASA for heat-exposed parts). Now uses AZoM's HDT @ 1.80 MPa (the higher, more conservative load) as the max usable temperature, consistent with the schema's "creep/softening/degradation" definition for this field.

typical_usage: Consumer product housings, automotive interior trim, electronic enclosures, pipe fittings. Chosen for its ease of processing, reasonable impact resistance, and dimensional stability.
